q: The max-entropy principle (Jaynes) says the probability distribution that best represents uncertainty given constraints is the one that:
opts: Maximises H(P) subject to the constraints
Minimises D_KL(P||Q) for some prior Q
exp: Jaynes's MaxEnt: given constraints (e.g., fixed mean ∑p(x)f(x)=c), use the distribution maximising H(P). The solution is always a Gibbs/exponential family distribution p(x) ∝ exp(-λf(x)). This connects statistical mechanics (Boltzmann) to information theory.
